You are the referee of a simulated phone call between a CALLER and a customer-service AGENT.
For each numbered condition, decide whether it is met RIGHT NOW, judging mainly the agent's LATEST turn in light of the whole call.
- "the agent first ..." / "the first time ..." means it happens in the latest turn and had not happened before.
- Conditions about what the agent says are judged on its words. "[system actions: ...]" lists tools the agent used; use them only for conditions about what the agent does (e.g. "starts looking up").
- Conditions phrased as a caller stop rule (e.g. "Agent confirms ...", "End the call right after ...") are met when the call has reached that point.
- Be literal and strict: if in doubt, it is not met.
Reply with JSON only, one key per condition id: {"<id>": {"met": true|false, "why": "<at most 15 words>"}}

CALL SO FAR:
CALLER: Hi, Kevin Brooks. We moved to Gahanna, and I want to move all of our family's prescriptions from the East Broad store to the Gahanna store for good.
AGENT: Hi Kevin, I'd be happy to help you move your family's prescriptions to Gahanna. Let me first verify your identity, and then we'll get everything set up. Can you give me your date of birth?
CALLER: August 30th, 1982. So once that's confirmed, can we get all three of us switched over today?
AGENT: Great, Kevin, you're verified. I can help with that. Just to clarify—when you say all three of you, are those two other family members, and do they have prescriptions at the East Broad store as well?  [system actions: verify_identity]
CALLER: Right, three of us total. Mine's the lisinopril, Maya's got the albuterol inhaler, and Eli's on Vyvanse. All at East Broad right now.
AGENT: Perfect. Before I move things over, I need to verify the other two family members' names and dates of birth so I can set up their pharmacy changes and handle their prescriptions. Can you give me Maya's full name and date of birth?
CALLER: Sure, Maya Brooks, June 20th, 2017. And Eli Brooks is February 11th, 2010.
AGENT: Thanks. Let me verify Maya and Eli so we can get everyone switched over. Excellent, everyone's verified. Now let me pull up all your prescriptions so I can see what we're moving. Good news—I can move Kevin's lisinopril and Maya's albuterol right away. But Eli's Vyvanse is a controlled medication that's already been filled, so we'll need a new prescription from Dr. Okafor to move that one. Let me first find the Gahanna store and then get everything set up. Perfect. Now I'll set Gahanna as the home pharmacy for all three of you and move the prescriptions that can move today.  [system actions: verify_identity, verify_identity, list_prescriptions, list_prescriptions, list_prescriptions, find_stores]
CALLER: Wait, why not the Vyvanse? Okay, so what's the plan for Eli?
AGENT (LATEST): Good question. Eli's Vyvanse is a C-II controlled medication that's already been filled, so it can't be transferred or refilled as-is—we need a brand new prescription from Dr. Okafor to move it to Gahanna. Here's what I'll do: I'll set up Gahanna as Eli's home pharmacy and move the other two prescriptions today, then I'll request a new Vyvanse prescription from Dr. Okafor to send to Gahanna. Does that work for you?

CONDITIONS:
stop_0: Agent recaps: two moved, defaults set, Vyvanse new-Rx request to Dr. Okafor.
emergency: In its LATEST turn, the agent told the caller to hang up and call 911 (or emergency services) now.

JSON only.
